analysis.evidence: הָעַיִט names the birds of prey as the subject, and עַל הַפְּגָרִים gives their destination, “onto the carcasses.” Abram then drives the birds away.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with the collective singular subject הָעַיִט.

draft.change: Add the masculine noun עַיִט under עיט with its bird-of-prey sense and document its collective use.
draft.definition: A bird of prey that may feed on carrion.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 15:11 the birds descend on the carcasses and Abram drives them away.

analysis.evidence: The singular verb וַיֵּרֶד agrees with הָעַיִט as the subject descending on the carcasses. When Abram drives the birds away, the plural object אֹתָם refers back to them, showing that the singular noun denotes a group.
analysis.morphology: הָ is the definite article before ע. עַיִט is a masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, used collectively here.
analysis.sense: Bird of prey, here one that feeds on carrion.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּרֶד הָעַיִט עַל הַפְּגָרִים, עַל introduces the carcasses as the place upon which the bird of prey descended.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.
